title: General Project Manifest Schema
description: Manifest for non-software projects (academic, creative, business, personal). Describes project identity, structure, deliverables, and context.
$comment: This schema is intentionally open (no additionalProperties:false). Add sections that best manifest your project's content. Examples: 'research_methodology' for academic, 'brand_guidelines' for creative, 'market_analysis' for business.

project.description: Basic identity, purpose, and timeline of the project.
project.$comment: Core project information. Adapt fields to your domain: academic (thesis title, institution), creative (client, campaign), business (company, market).

name.$comment: Examples: 'Master Thesis: AI in Healthcare', 'Brand Redesign for Acme Corp', 'Q4 Marketing Campaign'.

description.description: High-level description of what this project aims to achieve.
description.$comment: STOP: ONE sentence — what the project produces and for whom. REDIRECT: detailed structure, phase breakdowns, methodology, package/tool lineage go in structure/standards, NOT here. If you name a tool or methodology, that clause belongs in standards. bad→good: Bad: 'Tesis organizada en 6 capítulos siguiendo metodología cualitativa, con datos de...'. Good: 'Tesis de maestría sobre IA en salud para el comité de la universidad.'

start_date.$comment: When work on this project began. Use best estimate if exact date unknown.

target_date.$comment: Optional. Deadline or target completion date if applicable.

stakeholders.description: People or entities involved or interested in the project.
stakeholders.$comment: Examples: 'Prof. García (thesis advisor)', 'Marketing Team', 'Client: Acme Corp', 'Investors'.

structure.description: Organization of the project: sections, chapters, phases, or components.
structure.$comment: Adapt to your project type. Academic: chapters/sections. Creative: deliverables/assets. Business: phases/milestones.

components.description: List of main components, sections, or phases.

name.$comment: STOP: a short noun-phrase a non-technical person recognizes (<=~60 chars), like 'Chapter 1: Introduction', 'Phase 1: Discovery', 'Logo Design'. REDIRECT: status goes in status, dependencies in dependencies, the what-it-covers prose in description — NOT here. If you wrote ':' followed by an explanation, that explanation belongs in description.

description.description: Brief description of this component's purpose.
description.$comment: What this component covers or delivers.

dependencies.description: Other components this one depends on.
dependencies.$comment: Optional. List names of components that must be completed first.

deliverables.description: Concrete outputs or artifacts the project will produce.

name.$comment: STOP: a short noun-phrase a non-technical person recognizes (<=~60 chars), like 'Final Thesis Document', 'Brand Guidelines PDF', 'Pitch Deck'. REDIRECT: format goes in format, contents/purpose prose in description, deadline in due_date — NOT here. If you wrote ':' followed by an explanation, that explanation belongs in description.

description.description: What this deliverable contains or represents.
description.$comment: Brief description of content and purpose.

due_date.$comment: Optional. Specific deadline for this deliverable.

deliverables.$comment: List all expected outputs. Academic: thesis, presentations. Creative: designs, assets. Business: reports, decks.

references.description: Reference materials, sources, and resources for the project.
references.$comment: Organize references by type. Adapt categories to your domain.

urls.$comment: Examples: 'https://competitor.com', 'Shared Google Drive folder', 'Figma project link'.

bibliography.$comment: For academic projects. Use consistent citation format (APA, MLA, etc.).

standards.description: Guidelines, standards, or methodologies the project follows.
standards.$comment: Reference your project_standards.json or list key standards inline.

style_guide.$comment: Examples: 'APA 7th Edition', 'Company Brand Guidelines v2', 'Chicago Manual of Style'.

relations.description: The semantic blast-radius graph: directed edges that say 'a change to X can affect Y' — the dependencies a plain file listing cannot see (e.g. a survey deliverable feeds the final report; the brand guidelines guard every design asset).

from.description: The source element the edge starts at — the one whose change can affect the target.
from.$comment: STOP: name an element that EXISTS elsewhere in this manifest — a deliverable, a structure section, a reference, a standard. REDIRECT: do not invent free-floating labels; the graph is only navigable if from/to resolve to real manifest entries. bad: 'the research part'. good: 'literature-review' (a declared deliverable).

to.description: The target element the edge points at — the one affected when 'from' changes.
to.$comment: Same discipline as 'from': a real element named elsewhere in the manifest. The edge reads from-kind-to: e.g. 'survey-results' feeds 'final-report'.

kind.description: The edge verb — HOW 'from' relates to 'to'. Open vocabulary; pick the most precise.
kind.$comment: Suggested verbs (OPEN — add others when none fit; recurring ones get officialized via the corpus miner): feeds (produces input the other uses), depends_on (cannot proceed without it), guards (constrains/gates — a standard, a brand rule, an approval), informs (shapes a decision), supersedes (replaces). STOP: one lowercase verb, not a sentence — the sentence is 'why'.

why.description: The one-line reason this edge matters for blast-radius — what breaks or changes in 'to' when 'from' changes.
why.$comment: STOP: the consequence, not a restatement of the verb. This is the WHOLE point of the edge. bad: 'survey feeds report' (restates from/kind/to). good: 'if the survey sample changes, the report's headline statistics must be recomputed'. REDIRECT: one cause→effect clause, no essays.

relations.$comment: OPTIONAL but high-value — the manifest's reason to exist beyond a deliverables list: an element's blast-radius at a glance, especially when scoping a logbook. STOP: only edges a plain listing CANNOT show — cross-deliverable/cross-standard couplings. REDIRECT: a deliverable simply belonging to a phase is not an edge; capture genuine 'change here forces change there' couplings. Born-compliant (product_rule #13): extra edge fields are allowed (the item is open) — recurring extras are officialization candidates surfaced by the corpus miner.

notes.$comment: Flexible section for anything that doesn't fit elsewhere.

risks.$comment: Examples: 'Tight deadline', 'Pending client approval', 'Data collection delays'.

assumptions.description: Assumptions the project is based on.
assumptions.$comment: Examples: 'Client will provide brand assets by Nov 15', 'Survey will reach 100+ respondents'.

recommendations.description: Suggestions for improvement or next steps.
